question: You're starting an antenatal chat with an expectant mum. Which simple action instantly helps build trust without saying a word?

options.A: Writing notes continuously during the conversation
options.B: Sitting down at eye level with the patient
options.C: Standing over the bed while asking questions
options.D: Crossing arms tightly across the chest

explanation: Sitting down shows openness and respect! It instantly tells the mum you have time for her, which helps lower her anxiety during the visit. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do body language and a gentle touch matter so much when you're caring for a woman in labor?

options.A: Patients often rely on body language and touch more than spoken instructions during vulnerable moments
options.B: Hospital regulations require midwives to maintain strict physical distance
options.C: It completely replaces the need for taking a formal verbal health history
options.D: Verbal language is rarely understood by patients in rural clinics

explanation: When a mum is stressed, in pain, or vulnerable, a reassuring touch or warm facial expression carries way more emotional comfort than spoken words alone. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the main reason for creating a calm, private space when taking a patient's history?

options.A: To allow patients to share intimate health details without fear of judgment
options.B: To speed up the hospital discharge process for stable mothers
options.C: To reduce the number of required nursing documentation forms
options.D: To ensure the consulting room looks modern and well-equipped

explanation: A safe, private space encourages openness. When mums know their privacy is protected, they feel comfortable sharing sensitive health information honestly. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h2)

question: Picture this: you're interviewing a teenage mother in a busy, noisy Nigerian antenatal clinic. What's your best next move?

options.A: Conduct the entire interview loudly so the patient speaks up
options.B: Postpone the health history interview until the patient delivers
options.C: Move behind a privacy screen or find a quiet corner to protect confidentiality
options.D: Ask a relative to answer all the sensitive questions instead

explanation: Even when clinic space is tight, protecting physical and emotional privacy is a must so the young mum feels safe talking to you. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which of these questions is a classic open-ended question that gets a patient talking?

options.A: Are you experiencing any vaginal bleeding right now?
options.B: How have you been feeling since your last antenatal visit?
options.C: Did you take your routine malaria prophylaxis today?
options.D: How many previous pregnancies have you carried to term?

explanation: Spot on! Asking how someone has been feeling invites a full story, whereas the others can easily be answered with a quick yes, no, or a single number. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why should you avoid asking 'leading' questions (like 'You've been taking your iron meds every day, right?') during an interview?

options.A: Hospital policy strictly bans the use of adjectives in medical records
options.B: Leading questions take too much time to answer compared to closed questions
options.C: They automatically violate patient confidentiality regulations
options.D: Patients may give the answer they think the midwife wants to hear rather than the truth

explanation: Leading questions subtly pressure the patient to agree with us. We want honest answers so we can give the right care! [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h3)

question: When taking a complete health history, a great midwife goes beyond physical vital signs to also explore what?

options.A: The patient's personal financial bank statements
options.B: Past employment records of the patient's grandparents
options.C: Detailed architectural layouts of the patient's home
options.D: Psychosocial needs, support systems, and emotional stress

explanation: Good midwifery care is holistic! We always want to check on her emotional well-being, home support, and stress levels alongside her physical health. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h4)

question: An antenatal mum's blood pressure stays high despite her medication, but she has no physical complaints. What should you gently explore next?

options.A: The structural durability of her residential building
options.B: Her spouse's exact occupational title and salary grade
options.D: Psychosocial stressors, home environment, and domestic support

explanation: Sometimes stubborn high blood pressure is tied to hidden emotional stress or trouble at home. Digging a little deeper with empathy makes all the difference. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the true heart and goal of counselling a patient in midwifery practice?

options.A: To force patients to follow strict hospital rules without questioning
options.B: To replace routine medical examinations with talk therapy
options.C: To diagnose complex psychiatric illnesses independently
options.D: To empower patients to make informed decisions about their own health

explanation: Counselling isn't about giving orders; it's about walking alongside the client so she feels confident and informed about her own body and choices. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h5)

question: How is professional counselling different from just telling a patient what they should do?

options.A: Counselling guides the client to find their own solutions rather than imposing the midwife's opinion
options.B: Counselling is performed only by licensed medical doctors in private clinics
options.C: Giving direct advice requires active listening, whereas counselling does not
options.D: Counselling is reserved exclusively for postpartum psychosis cases

explanation: Instead of bossing patients around, true counselling helps them think through options so they own their health decisions. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h5)

question: You encounter a language barrier during a clinic consultation. What is the safest, most respectful way to handle it?

options.A: Use a qualified interpreter or bilingual staff member
options.B: Ask the patient's young child to translate all medical terms
options.C: Skip the health history interview entirely
options.D: Speak very loudly and slowly in English

explanation: Using a trained translator or a colleague who speaks the language ensures nothing gets lost in translation while keeping the patient's dignity intact. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is it a big mistake to mock or dismiss a patient's traditional cultural beliefs?

options.A: It proves the midwife lacks a university degree
options.B: It makes the patient feel judged or disrespected, causing them to hide important health practices
options.C: It automatically breaks federal hospital administration laws
options.D: It stops the patient from paying required hospital user fees

explanation: When mums feel judged, they stop telling us about herbal teas or traditional remedies they might be taking, which could affect their care. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which ethical principle gives a fully competent patient the right to say 'no' to a recommended treatment?
explanation: Autonomy means self-governance. Every patient has the legal and moral right to make their own final choices about their body. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h7)

question: As a midwife, patient confidentiality is sacred. When is it legally and ethically okay to break it?

options.A: Whenever a curious family member asks about the patient's diagnosis
options.B: Whenever the clinic waiting room is overcrowded
options.C: When the midwife wants to discuss difficult cases with friends outside work
options.D: When there is a serious safety risk such as suspected child abuse or imminent harm

explanation: We protect secrets fiercely, but safety always comes first. If there's danger like abuse or imminent self-harm, breaking confidentiality to protect life is necessary. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the main reason we keep clear, accurate written notes during midwifery care?

options.A: To ensure continuity of care across different shifts and health workers
options.B: To replace verbal handovers during shift changes entirely
options.C: To serve as a punishment tool for non-compliant patients
options.D: To provide reading material for hospital inspectors

explanation: Good records mean that when you go off duty, the next midwife on shift knows exactly what was discussed and what care the mum needs next! [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h8)

question: You spot a pregnant woman with a severe complication who urgently needs specialist care. What completes this referral properly?

options.A: Writing a concise referral letter and communicating directly with the receiving facility
options.B: Discharging the patient immediately with a prescription for vitamins
options.C: Telling the patient to walk to the nearest general hospital alone
options.D: Documenting the refusal in the clinic logbook and closing the file

explanation: Safe referrals need teamwork! Writing a clear note and talking directly to the receiving hospital ensures the patient is expected and treated without dangerous delays. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h8)
